sampling: for each of CPVT / Long QT Syndrome / Brugada syndrome / Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy, the unique bound sentences were shuffled with seed 7 and the first 10 taken (HCM had only 9 unique); single annotator; the sample is one case, not the 11-case corpus
what_is_counted: Does the excerpted sentence work as a decision rule for the disease it was bound to? The seven-slot census (case74_relation_error_census.json) counted wrong RELATIONS; this path asserts no relation, so the failure mode moves to what got excerpted and to which disease it was attached.

automatic_over_the_whole_corpus.note: 1.3% of spans were not copied from the passage and were dropped by a substring check, i.e. hallucinated excerpts are cheap to detect; a hallucinated relation is not.

examples: CPVT: 'This cascade of events can be triggered by emotional or physical stress, exertion or bathing and, although previously phenotypically silent, can lead to syncope or SCD.'
LQTS: 'In the absence of reversible or acquired causes of QT prolongation, Long QT syndrome is diagnosed.'
Brugada: 'Traditionally, a spontaneously occurring or pharmacologically induced type 1 pattern establishes the diagnosis of Brugada syndrome.'

Brugada: 'Diagnosis relies on characteristic electrocardiographic findings, including right bundle branch block and ST-segment elevations in the right precordial leads (V1-V3), sometimes unmasked by fever or pharmacologic challenge.'
HCM: 'Echocardiography is the first-level imaging exam for HCM diagnosis, showing left ventricle hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction as main features.'
CPVT: ESC advocates restricting strenuous physical activity and competitive sports
Brugada: 'a drug challenge test may be indicated to unmask characteristic ST-segment elevations'
HCM: 'CMR can confirm morphological characteristics with higher accuracy ... than echocardiography'
workup_or_treatment_rule_valid_but_not_d.note: the excerpter's own use= field labels most of these correctly, so they are filterable

degenerate_table_row_or_form_field.note: chunked tables lose their header, so a row reads as a bare co-occurrence list; the seven-slot path hit the same rows and turned them into feature_of assertions

examples: CPVT got 'Common etiologies include prior myocardial infarction or ischemia; inherited channelopathies, such as LQTS; and structural heart diseases, including HCM, Brugada syndrome, and ARVC.' because the excerpter named the subject 'ventricular tachycardia'
CPVT got the LQTS Schwartz-score row 'Baseline HR QTc ‡ QTc ≤ 420 ms 0.5 ...' for the same reason
LQTS got 'Differential diagnoses include long QT syndrome, Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, pulmonary embolism, ...' which is the differential OF another disease
bound_to_the_wrong_disease.note: subject binding uses the same matcher as the mechanical engine, so this error is shared by both paths and is not fixed by dropping the slots

unusable_dangling_anaphora.example: LQTS: 'It is also indicated in those who have beta-blocker-resistant symptoms or have contraindications to beta-blockers.' — 'It' is resolved only in the preceding sentence, which was not excerpted

false_logical_claim.note: the point of the path: with no relation / modality / polarity slot there is nothing to overclaim. Compare 42/57 wrong required_for and 19/28 wrong pathognomonic_for in case74_relation_error_census.json.

LQTS_cutoff.seven_slot_path: 'A normal QTc in men is less than 440ms, and in women, it is less than 460ms.' was slotted as excludes+negated, which the engine cannot execute, so LQTS was never ruled out on QTc 380 ms
LQTS_cutoff.nl_path: the same sentence is carried verbatim, ranks 5th by corpus support in the LQTS block, and 'Long QT syndrome – QTc >0.450 sec' carries a program-parsed threshold {'operator': '>', 'value': 0.45, 'unit': 'sec'}

CPVT_trigger.seven_slot_path: split into bare test names (Holter, exercise testing, genetic testing) marked required_for+obligatory
CPVT_trigger.nl_path: 'This cascade of events can be triggered by emotional or physical stress, exertion or bathing ...' survives whole, but ranks 13th by support, below five treatment sentences about magnesium and β-blockers

summary.reading: The alternative path removes the error class the seven-slot schema is worst at (74% wrong relations on the high-stakes diagnostic slots) and replaces it with a benign one: four fifths of the excerpts are not decision rules, but nothing in them is false about the source. The two error classes are not equally harmful — a wrong required_for hard-eliminates a hypothesis, an off-topic sentence only costs context.
